name: Ameca
summary: Expressive humanoid for events, attractions and research; sold by quote and rented for events.
specs_note: Ameca is an expressive upper-body/interaction robot (base configuration does not walk); physical specs and mobility were not confirmed against an Engineered Arts primary source in this pass -> left NULL. Vision + conversational interaction are core Ameca features -> has_vision/has_language_ui true. Fields (height_cm, mobility, autonomy) were subsequently verified and ratified by the product owner during the 2026-08-18 duplicate-reconciliation review, superseding the earlier note that left them NULL pending a primary source. SPECIFICATIONS (HO-DATA Fast Lane batch 2, 2026-10-22): weight, total DoF and arm span from the Ameca specification table of Engineered Arts' own site (https://www.engineeredarts.com/robot/ameca/, a script-rendered page whose specification text is served in the site's own asset https://www.engineeredarts.com/assets/index-DwBa69-D.js; block 'model: Ameca, generation: 2.6 (2024)'). The table's height '1870 mm' matches the existing 187 cm. DoF is confirmed by Engineered Arts' user documentation https://docs.engineeredarts.co.uk/guide/reference/hardware/mesmer_full_size_gen2 ('Ameca … has 61 degrees of freedom'). The values describe the current generation 2.6; earlier Ameca builds may differ. Walking speed does not apply (Ameca does not walk; mobility STATIONARY). Payload and runtime are not stated; the robot runs from a mains 'Robot Power Supply'. All three stay UNKNOWN. commercial_status_evidence.note: COMMERCIAL: Ameca is generally available for sale (by quote) and event rental per the manufacturer site.

capabilities.detail: Human-like facial expression is Ameca's signature capability.
Conversational voice interaction for events and demos.

use_case_fits.notes: Purpose-built for expressive event/attraction engagement; available to buy or rent.
use_case_fits.limitations: Interaction-focused; base configuration does not perform physical manipulation/locomotion tasks.

use_case_fits.notes: Editorial judgement. Expressive face and conversational interaction make Ameca a platform for human-robot interaction studies; the catalogue summary lists research alongside events.
use_case_fits.limitations: Interaction research only: the base configuration does not walk or manipulate. Developer interfaces are not recorded.

use_case_fits.notes: Editorial judgement. Expressive face and conversational interaction suit greeting and information roles in a service environment.
use_case_fits.limitations: Interaction only: the base configuration does not walk or manipulate, so it cannot handle products. Not a demonstrated application: no deployment for this use is recorded.

spec_caveats.text: Engineered Arts' Ameca specification table states 'Weight 137.7 lbs | 62 kg' for model Ameca, generation '2.6 (2024)'.

Engineered Arts states '61 Degrees of Freedom (DoF)' for Ameca (generation 2.6). Its user documentation gives the same total: 27 face, 5 neck, 8 shoulders, 10 arms, 8 hands, 3 torso. Ameca does not walk, so no leg DoF are included.
Engineered Arts states 'Arm Span 70.9 in | 1800 mm' for Ameca (generation 2.6); 180 cm is a unit conversion.
Engineered Arts states '8 degrees of freedom in the hands, 4 left, 4 right' (https://docs.engineeredarts.co.uk/guide/reference/hardware/mesmer_full_size_gen2).
Engineered Arts states '"controlAPI":"REST, WebSocket, Python & Node.js SDKs"' (https://engineeredarts.com/assets/index-DwBa69-D.js).
